models.description: Heart disease risk check. Chest pain when walking or climbing stairs, chest discomfort on exertion, worried about my heart, blocked arteries, coronary artery disease, high cholesterol and heart risk, family history of heart problems.
models.name: Heart disease risk
models.trained_on: 782 people referred for heart tests at hospitals in the USA, Hungary and Switzerland (UCI Heart Disease data, 1980s), with disease confirmed by angiography
models.limitations: Not a diagnosis and not for chest pain happening now. It estimates blocked heart arteries among people who were already sent for heart tests, so it may not fit the general public. It uses no ECG or scan results. Data is from the 1980s and has no Indian patients. Quality varied between hospitals: AUC Cleveland (USA) 0.839, Budapest (Hungary) 0.883, Switzerland 0.784, Long Beach VA (USA) 0.75. Scores are scaled so 50% is the flagging point. An ECG and a doctor's visit are the real next step.

Trained only on adult Pima women in the USA, on a small dataset, so it is less reliable for men and for Indian patients. Set to miss few cases: in our test it caught 94% of people with diabetes but also flagged 44% of people without it, so a Higher risk result often turns out fine after testing. models.trained_on: 5,700 pregnancies from a dataset of early-pregnancy lab results (source not named by the repo; about a third of the rows look synthetic)
models.limitations: Not a diagnosis; a glucose tolerance test confirms gestational diabetes. With the full lab panel it scored well on held-out rows, but with only fasting sugar, age and BMI (the usual case here) it found 80% of cases and flagged half of healthy pregnancies, AUC 0.75. Fasting sugar is itself part of how this condition is diagnosed. Population and source unknown, and about a third of the training rows look synthetic. Not tested on Indian women. Scores are scaled so 50% is the flagging point. Please follow your obstetrician's screening plan whatever this says.

On 171 held-out Indian patients it caught 93% of liver patients but also flagged 78% of people without liver disease, so 'needs a closer look' is common and often turns out fine. AUC 0.77 is below our 0.80 bar, so it is shown as Unverified. On German patients it caught only 65%, so a 'less concerning' result does NOT rule out liver disease. Show abnormal reports to a doctor whatever this says.

Chest X-ray check. For people who have a chest X-ray, a lung X-ray or a chest scan image from a hospital or clinic and want it looked at. Cough, fever, breathlessness, chest infection, pneumonia, tuberculosis worry, lung patch, opacity or shadow on an X-ray report, fluid in the lungs, enlarged heart on X-ray. Needs an X-ray image upload.
models.name: Chest X-ray findings
models.upload_instructions: Upload one frontal chest X-ray. Crop to the X-ray and avoid glare if it is a photo of a film or screen.
models.trained_on: Base model: adult X-rays from NIH ChestX-ray14, PadChest, CheXpert, MIMIC-CXR, Google, OpenI and RSNA. Screening layers trained by the Curanex team on 4,825 VinBigData adult X-rays (Vietnam) and 4,171 Kermany child X-rays (China, ages 1-5).
models.limitations: Screening aid only, not a diagnosis; only a doctor can read an X-ray. Measured on held-out images: adults, abnormal X-ray check sensitivity 0.91, specificity 0.90; adult lung opacity check sensitivity 0.93, specificity 0.63, so about 4 in 10 X-rays without lung opacity still get flagged. Children, pneumonia check sensitivity 0.94, specificity 0.83, tested only on ages 1-5. X-rays came from a few hospitals in Vietnam and China, so accuracy in India is unknown. The test mix had more abnormal X-rays than everyday patients do. Opacity can have causes other than infection. A normal result does not rule out disease. Photos of films or screens lower accuracy. Scores are scaled so 50% is the flagging point; they are not percent chances of disease. In a separate test, a similar adult layer trained in one country fell to AUC 0.70 in another, so these adult results may not hold at other hospitals.
models.credit: Trained by the Curanex team using the method from TorchXRayVision (Cohen et al., mlmed/torchxrayvision), on VinBigData and Kermany 2018

metrics.eval_set: Headline: adult abnormal X-ray check on the held-out 15% of VinBigData (n=1035). Split by image, as patient ids are not available. Thresholds chosen on validation data.

models.status_note: Passes the switch-on bar with the trained layers (sensitivity and AUC >= 0.80 on held-out data). The base model alone did not.

models.name: DME check (retinal OCT scan)
models.trained_on: 55,656 retinal OCT scans (Kermany 2018), graded by eye specialists; whole network fine-tuned on a Kaggle GPU; flagging threshold set once on OCTDL (Russia)
models.limitations: Not a diagnosis. Needs an OCT scan (the grey cross-section image), not a retina photo. On a separate hospital's scans it found 83% of DME scans and flagged 0% of normal scans. People with diabetes need a yearly eye check.
models.credit: Trained by the Curanex team on Kermany et al. 2018; threshold set on OCTDL (Kulyabin et al. 2024); tested on Duke / Srinivasan et al. 2014; ImageNet EfficientNet-B0 fully fine-tuned on a Kaggle GPU
models.status_note: Verified on Duke (USA), never used before: eye level sensitivity 1.0, AUC 1.0; scan level sensitivity 0.826, AUC 0.971.
models.description: Diabetic macular oedema (DME) check from a retinal OCT scan. Swelling of the macula, fluid in the retina, blurred central vision with diabetes.
